What does this Rocket setting do?

Search the label, an internal ID or a symptom, then match the feature and material scope. Read the introduction before using a test.

Working reference: 470 schema fields. 184 additional renderer controls still need exact labels/paths; this is not exhaustive runtime UI acceptance. Input bounds are not safe hardware ratings.


Mask type

action-mask-rule
action-mask-rule:maskType

What does it mean? Chooses what a modifier or mask region is intended to affect. A mask is an auxiliary region, not automatically a printable part.

When would I change it? When deliberately restricting support or applying a documented regional modifier, not during a basic material comparison.

What happens if I adjust it? Changing the class can change which toolpaths are permitted in the region. It does not simply change the colour of the region.

  • Support blocker: A region intended to prevent support generation where it intersects. It does not make an unsupported overhang printable without support.
    Schema contexts: action-mask-rule
  • Support enforcer: A region intended to request support. Other support eligibility and geometry rules may still matter; verify the preview rather than assuming support appears everywhere.
    Schema contexts: action-mask-rule
  • Internal mask: Selects the internal-mask class. The precise roles and boundary treatment affected are unresolved in this survey; do not assume it cuts a cavity or changes a tool.
    Schema contexts: action-mask-rule
  • Full mask: Selects the full-mask class. Its exact difference from internal mask is not verified; do not assume it removes the model or applies every setting throughout it.
    Schema contexts: action-mask-rule

Check with: Mask placement and intersections; Support generation and regional settings

Internal-mask versus full-mask coverage is not established by these labels; inspect the resulting preview. The option names below are source labels, not a live visibility guarantee.

Schema-backed selector; partly interpreted; mask-class details unverified. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

What does it mean? Identifies this mask rule so a person can distinguish its purpose from other modifiers.

When would I change it? When naming or revising a rule, using a description such as the region and intended support action.

What happens if I adjust it? A clearer name improves traceability; the name alone is not evidence that the mask has the intended geometry or settings.

Check with: Mask type; Saved project identity

The editor control type was not resolved. Do not infer an automatic operation from a descriptive name.

Build plate temperature

CFC composite material / Temperature
composite-settings:bedTemperature

What does it mean? The requested build-plate temperature for normal composite printing, in degrees Celsius.

When would I change it? During a controlled adhesion or thermal-management comparison for the approved matrix/fibre pair and actual plate.

What happens if I adjust it? Higher can improve adhesion but increase bottom deformation and heat exposure; lower may reduce those effects but allow lifting.

Units: °C

Check with: First-layers bed temperature; Plate preparation and chamber condition

A temperature field is not a plate or material rating. Do not use bed heat to compensate for a loose plate or leaking hotend.

Functional interpretation; physical result unvalidated. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Build plate temp. on first layers

CFC composite material / Temperature
composite-settings:bedTemperatureOnFLs

What does it mean? The build-plate temperature requested during the initial-layer stage of the composite material.

When would I change it? Only after first-layer geometry and plate preparation are correct, when comparing initial adhesion.

What happens if I adjust it? More initial heat may help attachment but can enlarge or soften bottom features. Less may reduce flare but weaken attachment.

Units: °C

Check with: Normal bed temperature; Initial-layer stage and nozzle-to-plate relationship

The exact transition trigger must be checked in output; do not assume this follows the fan-height or nozzle-temperature-height field identically.

Label-based thermal interpretation; transition details unverified. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Chamber temperature

CFC composite material / Temperature
composite-settings:chamberTemperature

What does it mean? The requested chamber temperature for the composite material, where the machine supports active chamber heating.

When would I change it? When qualifying the approved material pair's enclosure conditions, within current machine and material guidance.

What happens if I adjust it? A warmer environment can reduce thermal contraction but may worsen small details, feed-path heat exposure or cooling balance.

Units: °C

Check with: Heated-chamber capability and index; Exhaust and part cooling

Entering a target does not prove a chamber heater exists, its sensor is correct or the target was reached. Never change hardware capability flags to force heating.

Functional interpretation; hardware operation not tested. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Color

CFC composite material / BasicInformation
composite-settings:color

What does it mean? The colour assigned to the composite material's on-screen representation.

When would I change it? To make the selected material identifiable and keep the visual record consistent with the intended spool.

What happens if I adjust it? Changes the representation; it does not dye the part, load a fibre or prove which physical spool is installed.

Check with: Material name; Preview and physical spool record

Colour additives can affect real tuning, but changing this swatch does not retune temperature or flow.

Presentation interpretation; no physical qualification. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Fiber cost per spool ({symbol})

CFC composite material / OTHER
composite-settings:costPerSpool

What does it mean? Purchase cost for one continuous-fibre spool, in the application's selected currency.

When would I change it? When recording a different price or spool product for cost reporting.

What happens if I adjust it? Can change estimated material cost. A higher entered price is not stronger or faster fibre.

Check with: Fibre spool length; Estimated fibre consumption

The currency placeholder in the source label is dynamic. Cost metadata is not proof of loaded material or route eligibility.

Accounting interpretation; exact costing formula unverified. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Enable preheat

CFC composite material / Temperature
composite-settings:enablePreheat

What does it mean? Enables the composite material's separate nozzle-preheat behaviour.

When would I change it? Only when the supported OEM preparation sequence calls for a separate preheat stage.

What happens if I adjust it? Enabling may request the configured preheat temperature before printing; disabling does not itself prove the nozzle stays cold.

Check with: Extruder preheat temperature; Printer preparation and standby routines

Do not disable preparation requirements to bypass a loading problem. Actual timing and waits must be checked in the supported workflow.

Label-based switch interpretation; lifecycle timing unverified. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Enable print cooling

CFC composite material / Cooling
composite-settings:enablePrintCooling

What does it mean? Allows the composite material's print-cooling schedule to control its assigned part-cooling fan.

When would I change it? During a documented cooling comparison, not to silence an unidentified fan.

What happens if I adjust it? Enabling allows the configured initial and regular cooling requests; disabling does not prove every machine fan stops.

Check with: First-layers and regular fan speeds; Composite tool fan mapping

This is not authority to stop a protective hotend heatsink fan. Confirm the physical fan role before changing it.

Functional interpretation; fan routing requires hardware verification. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Extra unretract length

CFC composite material / Retraction
composite-settings:extraLengthP

What does it mean? Additional matrix-plastic feed associated with unretraction, beyond restoring the ordinary retracted amount.

When would I change it? Only after supported composite retraction is understood and repeated restarts show a genuine matrix shortage.

What happens if I adjust it? More can fill a lean restart but create a blob or excess pressure; less can reduce buildup but leave a gap.

Units: mm

Check with: Matrix retract length; Unretract speed and temperature

This is matrix plastic, not continuous-fibre length or a repair for leakage. Exact restart application must be checked in output.

Label-based material interpretation; restart algorithm unverified. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Extra unretract on tool change

CFC composite material / Retraction
composite-settings:extraLengthPOnToolChange

What does it mean? Additional matrix-plastic feed associated specifically with recovery after a tool change.

When would I change it? When a verified tool-change test, rather than ordinary travel, shows a repeatable matrix restart deficit.

What happens if I adjust it? Increasing can improve an underfed return but add a blob; decreasing can reduce over-priming while risking starvation.

Units: mm

Check with: Tool-change retract length; Standby temperature and before/after tool-change code

Do not copy an ordinary plastic value here or use this to alter the continuous-fibre loading cycle.

Functional interpretation; complete tool lifecycle unvalidated. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Plastic flow multiplier

CFC composite material / BasicInformation
composite-settings:extrusionMultiplierP

What does it mean? Scales the matrix-plastic amount commanded for the composite material; it is separate from continuous-fibre feed.

When would I change it? For a supported, controlled matrix-flow comparison with the approved pair and loading state held fixed.

What happens if I adjust it? Higher requests more matrix and may improve coverage or cause buildup; lower requests less and can leave a poorly wetted or underfilled route.

Check with: Plastic filament diameter; Fibre route geometry, temperature and speed

A multiplier is not a safe pressure limit or proof that empty-fibre operation is supported. Do not infer a fibre percentage from it.

Functional interpretation; actual composite deposition unvalidated. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Fiber extrusion speed

CFC composite material / RESTART
composite-settings:extrusionSpeedF

What does it mean? Fibre-feed speed in the composite material's restart settings, measured as strand length per second.

When would I change it? Only under a supported composite restart procedure after the physical path and loading state are proven.

What happens if I adjust it? A faster feed changes the restart's delivery rate; it is not necessarily the speed of every reinforced model route.

Units: mm/s

Check with: Fibre restart length; Restart lift, pause and matrix delivery

Do not treat this as ordinary plastic print speed. Excessive strand feeding can buckle, tangle or misplace fibre; exact scheduling is unverified.

Restart-context interpretation; exact execution unverified. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Unretract speed

CFC composite material / Retraction
composite-settings:extrusionSpeedP

What does it mean? The speed used to restore retracted matrix plastic, not the toolhead's model-printing speed.

When would I change it? After distance is stable, if supported matrix restart tests show a speed-related gap or surge.

What happens if I adjust it? Faster restoration can recover pressure sooner but demand more from the feed system; slower may reduce the surge but delay recovery.

Units: mm/s

Check with: Matrix retract length and extra unretract; Nozzle temperature and tool-change preparation

Do not copy ordinary FFF unretract settings to this path without an approved composite comparison.

Label-based retraction interpretation; physical response unvalidated. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

What happens if I adjust it? May affect material calculations or compatibility assumptions. It does not physically resize the guide or nozzle.

Units: mm

Do not falsify the diameter to change feed or force an unsupported strand through the system; exact downstream use is unverified.

Finish ironing distance

CFC composite material / RESTART
composite-settings:finishIroningDistance

What does it mean? A distance in the composite restart/finish settings associated with ironing or pressing a route end.

When would I change it? Only during an OEM-supported composite end/restart investigation with the route and loading state fixed.

What happens if I adjust it? A longer distance can extend end treatment; a shorter one can leave less treatment. Exact path, timing and feed behaviour are not established here.

First layers fan speed height

CFC composite material / Cooling
composite-settings:firstLayersFanHeight

What does it mean? The height in millimetres over which the composite initial-layer fan setting is intended to apply.

When would I change it? When isolating early-layer cooling after adhesion and the supported composite baseline are reliable.

What happens if I adjust it? A greater height keeps the initial cooling condition over more of the part; it does not mean that many numbered layers.

Units: mm

Check with: Initial fan speed; Layer height and regular fan speed

Check the transition in output; rounding to layers and boundary inclusion are not verified. Do not confuse this with initial nozzle-temperature height.

First layers fan speed

CFC composite material / Cooling
composite-settings:firstLayersFanSpeed

What does it mean? The requested part-cooling percentage during the composite initial cooling stage.

When would I change it? For an early-layer adhesion/curl comparison while preserving the correct fan mapping.

What happens if I adjust it? More cooling can sharpen edges but weaken attachment or bonding; less retains heat but may permit curling or soft features.

Units: %

Check with: Initial fan height; Plate, chamber and regular cooling

A percentage is not measured airflow. This must not be confused with a hotend-protection fan.

Functional interpretation; airflow and physical result unvalidated. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

First layers temp. height

CFC composite material / Temperature
composite-settings:firstLayersHeight

What does it mean? The height in millimetres associated with using the composite initial-layer nozzle temperature.

When would I change it? When comparing how long the initial thermal condition should persist after a reliable first layer.

What happens if I adjust it? Increasing extends that condition in height; decreasing switches toward normal printing temperature sooner.

Units: mm

Check with: Initial and normal nozzle temperatures; Layer height and heat history

This is a height, not a layer count. Verify the actual temperature transition and do not infer a separate bed/fan transition from it.

Linear density

CFC composite material / OTHER
composite-settings:linearDensity

What does it mean? Fibre mass per length, expressed in tex: grams per 1,000 metres of strand.

When would I change it? When defining a supported fibre product from its actual specification.

What happens if I adjust it? Changes the relationship between fibre length and estimated mass; it is not ordinary plastic density or a feed-speed percentage.

Units: tex = g/km

Check with: Fibre length and mass estimates; Fibre product and cost reporting

Do not enter grams per metre or plastic density in this field. Its exact use outside accounting remains unverified.

Machine/printer template / ACCELERATION
printer-settings:regularAcceleration

What does it mean? The general acceleration request used where a more specific feature setting does not control the move.

When would I change it? During supported motion qualification with a stable material baseline and representative geometry.

What happens if I adjust it? Higher can reduce time on short segments but add vibration/feed transients; lower can make motion gentler at a time cost.

Check with: Acceleration enable and per-feature values; Firmware limits and requested speed

Do not assume it overrides every role or raises firmware limits. A highest surviving sample is not automatically the best production setting.

Process: general / SUPPORT

What does it mean? The pattern used in the dense support contact region.

  • Rectilinear Interlaced: Straight-line interface filling with interlaced directions. It spreads contact across directions; inspect how layers alternate in Rocket.

  • Grid: Crossing line families forming a grid. This gives connections in more than one direction but creates intersections.

  • Line: Parallel straight fill paths. A simple directional fill; spacing and angle determine coverage.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / SUPPORT
  • Concentric: Nested paths following the region's outline. Useful when following contours matters; inspect narrow centers and corners.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / SUPPORT

Fiber infill pattern

Process: fortified / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: general / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDINFILL; profile-settings
profile-settings:infillFType

What does it mean? Selects the geometric pattern used for continuous-fibre infill.

When would I change it? Choose according to the reinforcement design rather than treating it as decorative plastic infill.

What happens if I adjust it? Different patterns create different rib directions, crossings, density distributions and continuous paths.

  • Solid: Uses solid-style fibre filling along the configured guide directions, rather than an open cellular rib pattern. It does not prove a void-free printed composite.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: general / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDINFILL; profile-settings
  • Rhombic grid: Uses two configured rib directions to form a diamond-like fibre network. The two angles control its directional layout.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: general / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDINFILL; profile-settings
  • Isogrid: Uses an isogrid-style triangular rib network. Its guide angle and density set orientation and spacing; no structural rating is implied.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: general / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDINFILL; profile-settings
  • Anisogrid: Uses a directionally arranged rib network with adjustable main-rib angles and crossing placement. It allows an intentionally unequal directional layout.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: general / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDINFILL; profile-settings
  • Tetragrid: Uses the named multi-rib grid with separate main-rib and side-slope angle controls. Preview those ribs together; the label alone does not define a tested layup.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: general / REINFORCEDINFILL; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDINFILL; profile-settings
  • Solid: Uses solid-style fibre filling along the configured guide directions, rather than an open cellular rib pattern. It does not prove a void-free printed composite.
    Schema contexts: profile-settings
  • Rhombic grid: Uses two configured rib directions to form a diamond-like fibre network. The two angles control its directional layout.
    Schema contexts: profile-settings
  • Isogrid: Uses an isogrid-style triangular rib network. Its guide angle and density set orientation and spacing; no structural rating is implied.
    Schema contexts: profile-settings
  • Anisogrid: Uses a directionally arranged rib network with adjustable main-rib angles and crossing placement. It allows an intentionally unequal directional layout.
    Schema contexts: profile-settings
  • Tetragrid: Uses the named multi-rib grid with separate main-rib and side-slope angle controls. Preview those ribs together; the label alone does not define a tested layup.
    Schema contexts: profile-settings

Check with: Pattern-specific angles and density; Fibre perimeters; Matrix structure

No listed pattern implies a load rating. Keep strand bending, anchoring and OEM process limits in scope.

profile-settings:infillPCellularFillAngle

What does it mean? Initial direction of fill lines for sparse plastic infill inside the part.

When would I change it? Change when line direction should suit a bridge span, surface appearance or load direction.

What happens if I adjust it? Rotates the pattern rather than making it denser; a different angle changes where lines meet walls.

Units: °

Patterns that are rotationally symmetric may respond differently. Confirm the selected region in Preview.

profile-settings:infillPCellularFillAngleStep

What happens if I adjust it? A larger step changes direction more per layer; zero requests no additional rotation.

Fill density

Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
profile-settings:infillPCellularFillDensity

What does it mean? The requested density of sparse plastic infill inside the part.

When would I change it? Increase when the interior needs more support or stiffness; reduce when material use and time matter more.

What happens if I adjust it? Higher density generally places lines closer together and uses more material; lower leaves larger voids.

Units: %

Declared editor constraints: {"integer": true}. These are input constraints, not operating recommendations or hardware limits.

Check with: Plastic infill pattern; Top solid layers; Wall count

Strength is direction- and geometry-dependent; density alone is not a structural qualification.

Fill pattern

Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
profile-settings:infillPCellularFillType

What does it mean? Shape of the paths used for sparse plastic infill inside the part.

When would I change it? Choose for support, directionality, appearance and practical print time.

What happens if I adjust it? Different patterns redirect material and change intersections and travel; they do not guarantee equal strength at equal nominal density.

  • Line: Parallel straight fill paths. A simple directional fill; spacing and angle determine coverage.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Grid: Crossing line families forming a grid. This gives connections in more than one direction but creates intersections.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Triangles: Three-direction line families forming triangular cells. Intersections and orientation affect the resulting structure and print behavior.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Zigzag: Back-and-forth fill joined where the geometry permits. It reduces separate line starts compared with disconnected lines.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Concentric: Nested paths following the region's outline. Useful when following contours matters; inspect narrow centers and corners.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Honeycomb: A cellular pattern based on hexagonal cells. It creates repeated cell walls rather than long parallel fill lines.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Tri-Hexagon: A pattern combining triangular and hexagonal regions. It changes cell geometry compared with a simple grid or honeycomb.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Gyroid: A smoothly varying three-dimensional periodic infill pattern. Layer shapes change through the height rather than repeating one flat grid.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • 3D Honeycomb: A honeycomb-style cellular structure that changes through the height. Inspect successive layers rather than judging it from one layer.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Cubic: A three-dimensional, cube-derived lattice. Its cross-section changes with height and distributes paths across several directions.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Crosshatch: A crossing-line hatch pattern. It changes the line arrangement and junction layout; compare the actual paths with Grid before choosing.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Diamond: A diamond-type triply periodic surface pattern: a repeating curved three-dimensional structure, not ordinary diamond-shaped straight ribs.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • TPMS-FK: The installed FK-named triply periodic surface option. It creates a repeating three-dimensional curved pattern; its exact parameterization is not established by the label.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Primitive: The Primitive-named triply periodic surface pattern, a repeating three-dimensional cell-and-connection geometry. It is distinct from adding a primitive model object.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Neovius: The Neovius-named triply periodic surface pattern. It offers a different repeating curved cell geometry; inspect channels and wall paths at the selected density.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Lidinoid: The Lidinoid-named triply periodic surface pattern. It offers another repeating curved three-dimensional geometry; density alone does not establish its strength.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Hilbert Curve: A winding, space-filling path with many right-angle turns. It produces a distinctive surface texture rather than a simple straight-line finish.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Archimedean Chords: A curved, spiral-derived fill layout. It changes the direction and visual texture of the fill; inspect the actual clipped paths.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings
  • Octagram Spiral: A star-like spiral fill layout. Its repeated turns give a distinctive path and surface pattern, not a guaranteed strength advantage.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: reinforced / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; Process: speedy / CELLULARPLASTICINFILL; profile-settings

Printing order

Process: general / WALLS; Process: reinforced / WALLS; Process: speedy / WALLS
profile-settings:inset0PrintOrder

What does it mean? Chooses whether the outer-wall sequence proceeds from the outside inward or from the inside outward.

When would I change it? Compare when exterior finish, dimensional consistency or overhang support needs attention.

What happens if I adjust it? The order changes which neighboring lines exist when a wall is laid down.

  • Outside in: Prints the outside wall first, then proceeds inward. This changes dimensional control and the support available beneath an overhanging outside line.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / WALLS; Process: reinforced / WALLS; Process: speedy / WALLS
  • Inside out: Prints inner wall paths before the outside wall. Existing inner lines may support the outside line but can also influence its final position.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / WALLS; Process: reinforced / WALLS; Process: speedy / WALLS

Check with: Wall count; Overhangs; Fibre printing order

No order is best for every shape. Inspect supported and unsupported outer contours separately.

Installed field declaration; plain-language functional interpretation; emitted behavior not validated · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Fiber shell calculation order

Process: fortified / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: general / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS
profile-settings:insetXFCalcOrder

What does it mean? Chooses whether fiber-shell paths are calculated from holes or from the outer contour first.

When would I change it? Use when competing fiber loops around holes and the outside need a different placement priority.

What happens if I adjust it? Holes first prioritizes hole-side shells; Contour first starts from the exterior. This concerns calculation priority, not a guaranteed visible print order.

  • Holes first: Prioritizes calculating the fiber shell from hole boundaries outward.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: general / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS
  • Contour first: Prioritizes calculating the fiber shell from the outer contour inward.
    Schema contexts: Process: fortified / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: general / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS

Check with: Fiber inner/outer counts; Available wall thickness; Fiber shell generation

Inspect the actual generated paths; narrow walls may not fit every requested loop.

profile-settings:organicTreeInterfaceSupportInfillType

    Schema contexts: Process: general / SUPPORT

profile-settings:organicTreeSupportXYDistance

What does it mean? Organic variant: Horizontal distance between tree supports and the model.

When would I change it? Use to reduce sidewall bonding or recover support near a boundary.

What happens if I adjust it? Larger clearance reduces side contact and available support area; smaller clearance brings branches closer.

Units: mm

Check with: Tree expansion; Branch routing; Top/bottom Z distances

It does not change vertical contact gaps. Inspect collision avoidance and overhang support together.

Installed schema/help supports this explanation; not physically print-validated. · Defined in installed schema; actual visibility and output remain conditional.

Outer contour expansion

Process: general / WALLS; Process: reinforced / WALLS; Process: speedy / WALLS
profile-settings:outerContourExpansion

What does it mean? XY offset applied to the part's outside contour for dimensional correction.

When would I change it? Use after flow is calibrated and measured outside dimensions show a repeatable offset.

What happens if I adjust it? Positive values enlarge the outside contour; negative values shrink it.

Units: mm

Check with: Hole expansion settings; Material shrinkage; Flow; Model dimensions

This changes contour dimensions, not overall scaling; verify holes and thin walls separately.

Extrusion width

profile-settings:overhangEWMM

When would I change it? Change to tune the path geometry after the material's base flow is sound.

What happens if I adjust it? Larger width asks for wider lines and more volume per unit path; smaller width requests narrower lines.

Units: mm

Check with: Material flow multiplier; Line width and layer height; Feature speed; Pattern and overlap

The requested width is not proof the nozzle can deliver it.

Flow multiplier

Process: general / OVERHANG; Process: reinforced / OVERHANG; Process: speedy / OVERHANG
profile-settings:overhangExtrusionMultP

What does it mean? Additional flow factor for overhang infill.

When would I change it? Change only when these paths alone need a measured flow correction.

What happens if I adjust it? It multiplies the material flow factor; increasing adds commanded plastic to these paths and decreasing reduces it.

Infill/Wall overlap

Process: general / OVERHANG; Process: reinforced / OVERHANG; Process: speedy / OVERHANG
profile-settings:overhangInfillExtendIntoPerimeterRatio

What does it mean? Fraction of line width by which overhang infill overlaps the surrounding perimeters.

When would I change it? Use when the skin-to-wall bond is incomplete or the boundary is excessively crowded.

What happens if I adjust it? Increasing grows the overlap; decreasing reduces intrusion into the perimeter region.

Check with: Line width; Perimeter geometry; Material and feature flow

This is a ratio, not millimeters or a direct percentage entry. Excess overlap can cause ridges.

Process: general / OVERHANG; Process: reinforced / OVERHANG; Process: speedy / OVERHANG
profile-settings:overhangSpeed

What does it mean? Requested print speed for overhang infill.

When would I change it? Change after temperature and flow are stable using a controlled feature-speed test.

What happens if I adjust it? Increasing raises motion and extrusion demand; decreasing reduces it and changes time/heat exposure.

Plastic extrusion compensation ratio

Process: fortified / REINFORCEDENTITIES; Process: general / REINFORCEDENTITIES; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDENTITIES
profile-settings:plasticExtrusionCompensationRatio

What does it mean? A ratio that multiplies the calculated plastic extrusion in reinforced-entity processing.

When would I change it? Use only when specifically validating this additional compensation layer.

What happens if I adjust it? Increasing adds calculated plastic; decreasing reduces it. It can combine with other flow corrections.

Seam distribution offset (fiber)

Process: fortified / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: general / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS
profile-settings:seamDistributionPositionOffsetFiber

What does it mean? Per-layer change of the fiber seam position, expressed as a fraction of the contour perimeter.

When would I change it? Use to spread or deliberately move fiber seams between layers.

What happens if I adjust it? Installed help describes each new layer moving by offset multiplied by perimeter: positive moves forward along the path and negative moves backward.

This is a perimeter-relative offset, not millimeters. Random seam settings may supersede specified placement.

Seam distribution type (fiber)

Process: fortified / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: general / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS; Process: reinforced / REINFORCEDPERIMETERS
profile-settings:seamDistributionPositionTypeFiber

What does it mean? Chooses random or specified fiber seam distribution positioning.

When would I change it? Use to trade a repeatable seam location against dispersing the fiber seam marks.

What happens if I adjust it? Random delegates position choice to random placement; Specified uses the related offset. Installed help says making either the start or distribution random can randomize both.

Check with: Fiber seam distribution offset; Fiber other seam-position type; Longest-edge fiber seam preference

Specified does not guarantee one absolute machine coordinate; contour geometry and other seam rules still apply.

What does it mean? Number of loops printed around the model as a skirt.

Support interface pattern

Process: general / SUPPORT
profile-settings:treeInterfaceSupportInfillType

What does it mean? Pattern used in tree-support contact-interface layers.

  • Line: Parallel line paths; compare line direction and boundary connections in Preview.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / SUPPORT
  • Concentric: Nested loops following the region boundary; ordinary fill-angle settings generally do not apply.
    Schema contexts: Process: general / SUPPORT

Check with: Interface spacing; Interface angles; Top/bottom layer count
